relations: partner_latitude / partner_longitude reset on address write

behavioral_notes.observation: geo_localize() iterates the selected partners (with_context lang='en_US'), builds an address string via base.geocoder.geo_query_address(street,zip,city,state,country) and calls _geo_localize -> geo_find, which dispatches on the configured provider's tech_name to _call_openstreetmap (default Nominatim) or _call_googlemap and performs an OUTBOUND HTTP GET to resolve the address to a (latitude, longitude) tuple. On success it writes partner_latitude, partner_longitude and date_localization=today; on failure (None) it accumulates the partner and pushes a 'danger' bus simple_notification listing the unmatched display_names. A first-pass full-address lookup falls back to a coarser city/state/country lookup if the precise one returns None. It is a no-op during import_file / current_test / registry-not-ready / install_demo unless force_geo_localize is set.

The active provider is resolved by _get_provider() from ir.config_parameter 'base_geolocalize.geo_provider' (a base.geo_provider id), falling back to the first base.geo_provider record. res.config.settings exposes geoloc_provider_id (config_parameter base_geolocalize.geo_provider) and geoloc_provider_googlemap_key (config_parameter base_geolocalize.google_map_api_key); get_google_map_api_key(env) sudo-reads that param. _call_googlemap raises a UserError if no API key is set and surfaces Google billing/error messages; provider method names are built dynamically (getattr(self,'_call_'+tech_name) and '_geo_query_address_'+provider), so adding a provider is a record + matching method, not metadata.

ResPartner.write() resets partner_latitude/partner_longitude to 0.0 whenever any of street/zip/city/state_id/country_id changes (and the geo fields are not themselves being set), so stale coordinates never outlive the address they were computed from. The module adds date_localization (Date, 'Geolocation Date') marking when the partner was last geocoded; partner_latitude/partner_longitude themselves live on the base res.partner. This keep-coordinates-consistent-with-address rule is pure Python, invisible to field metadata.

geo_find wraps the provider call: an AttributeError (no _call_<provider> method) raises UserError 'Provider %s is not implemented'; a propagated UserError is re-raised; any other Exception is swallowed (logged at debug) and returns None so a single bad address does not abort a batch. Inside the provider calls, transport exceptions go through _raise_query_error -> UserError('Error with geolocation server: ...'); non-200 responses are logged as warnings; Google ZERO_RESULTS returns None and non-OK status raises a UserError with billing guidance. _call_openstreetmap_reverse is explicitly disabled (raises UserError) under test_enable/current_test to avoid live network calls in CI.

No frontend assets: present=false, 0 JS files, 0 XML/OWL templates, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, no asset bundles. The only UI is one inherited res.config.settings form (provider + Google key) and the standard partner action that triggers geo_localize; all logic is server-side ORM + outbound HTTP.

3 outbound HTTP call sites in models/base_geocoder.py; SDK ['requests']; uses_api_keys=True (Google Maps geocoding key via ir.config_parameter base_geolocalize.google_map_api_key). Endpoints: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search (default forward geocode), https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse (reverse geocode for _get_localisation), https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json (Google provider). Nominatim calls send a User-Agent 'Odoo (http://www.odoo.com/contactus)' per OSM usage policy.

classification.rationale: base_geolocalize is a master-data enrichment / external-integration utility: it owns no business object of its own (only the technical base.geo_provider record and the base.geocoder AbstractModel) and exists to call an outside geocoding service to add latitude/longitude/date_localization to res.partner. By Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a pure 'support' value model — firm IT infrastructure (data enrichment via an external service interface), not a primary value-creating chain/shop/network activity: it transforms no document, resolves no customer engagement, and mediates no exchange between parties. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits best because the module is a data-management / external-integration service (provider configuration, API-key handling, outbound HTTP enrichment of master data). The category metadata says Sales/Sales (the data primarily feeds CRM/Sales mapping), but the module itself is infrastructure that enriches the partner record rather than running a sales activity, so 8.0 is chosen as the dominant character with the Sales consumption noted as context.

standard_capabilities: Forward geocoding of partner addresses to (lat,long) via OpenStreetMap Nominatim out of the box (no key)
Optional Google Maps geocoding provider (requires API key set in Settings)
Automatic stale-coordinate invalidation when a partner address changes
Batch geo_localize action with user notification of unmatched partners
typical_fits: Default OSM Nominatim geocoding with zero configuration for low-volume use
Switching to Google Maps by selecting the provider and entering the API key in Settings
Coordinates consumed downstream by CRM partner maps / territory assignment / nearest-partner search
common_gaps: Bulk / scheduled re-geocoding (no shipped cron; geo_localize is on-demand on selected records)
Nominatim usage-policy rate limiting (1 req/s, mandatory User-Agent) on large datasets — no built-in throttling/queue
Additional providers (HERE, Mapbox, Bing) require a new base.geo_provider record + matching _call_ method
Geocoding result quality/confidence is not stored — only the raw lat/long and a date
No caching of geocode results; identical addresses are re-queried each run
